issues.description: Collapsing working+walking into one state changes the DFS data model and the cycle-detection branch in push() needs an explicit invariant.
issues.detail: All three reviewers note the old state machine separated 'children queued' from 'currently descending', and push()'s LastIndexFunc cycle check reads that label. Merging them may be correct but is a behavioral change disguised as a rename. Write the DFS invariant down and verify the cycle-detection branch still holds.

issues.description: Cleanup moved from Sort() entry to defer changes the Sorter lifetime contract without documentation.
issues.detail: Previously state was cleared on next Sort() entry; now it's cleared when the iterator finishes. If Sort() is called but the returned iter.Seq is never invoked, stale state persists. The change is reasonable but the contract shift deserves a comment on the Sorter struct so the next reader does not revert it.

issues.description: sorted marker now only set when yield returns true, a semantic change on early termination that is undocumented.
issues.detail: Old code set s.state[k]=sorted unconditionally after pop; new code only sets it inside the yield-success branch. Likely safe because the defer wipes state, but this couples correctness to the defer and the commit message omits the change. State-machine changes need explicit justification.

issues.description: No regression test for the state-reuse bug the PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: The PR title is 'Fix state reuse' but the diff adds no test calling Sort() twice on the same Sorter and asserting the second result. A three-line regression test would lock in the contract the defer establishes and prevent silent reintroduction during the next refactor.

issues.description: Previous s.stack = s.stack[0:] was a no-op; new clear() + s.stack[:0] is correct but warrants a one-line comment.
issues.detail: s.stack[0:] sliced to full length and never reset the stack, leaving stale Node references that blocked GC. The fix is right: clear() nils pointer slots so the GC can reclaim them, then reslice to zero length. A short literate comment naming that intent would make it legible.

issues.description: Updated comment contains typos: 'visisted' and 'if its'.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged this. The comment is the load-bearing explanation of the two-visit DFS invariant, so it deserves the same care as the code. Fix to 'visited' and 'if it's'.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR fixes two real defects (s.stack[0:] was a no-op that retained Node references blocking GC; the sorted-marker placement and state cleanup were racy across reuse) but is under-audited and under-tested. The working/walking state collapse is a genuine data-model change, not a rename, and the cycle-detection branch in push() depends on a subtler invariant that must be written down. Cleanup-on-defer is the right call but the lifetime contract shift is undocumented, and the sorted-marker now depending on yield success is an undocumented semantic change. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — add a Sort()-twice regression test, document the invariant and contract changes, and fix the comment typos before landing.
